subject: maths
title: Percentages of Amounts: 10%, 15% of 360 and Percentage Problems
seo_title: Year 6 Percentages of Amounts Worksheets: Find 10%, 25%, 15% of 360, Measures and Sale Prices
standard_text: Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages [for example, of measures, and such as 15% of 360] and the use of percentages for comparison.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on percentages of amounts: find 50%, 25%, 10% and 1%, build 15% of 360 from 10% and 5%, find percentages of measures, work out 12 out of 50 as a percentage and solve sale price problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_sub: 5% is half of 10%, and 99% is 100% − 1%. To find what percentage a part is, make the total 100: 12 out of 50 = 24/100 = 24%.
body_html:
Per cent means “out of 100”

A percentage is a number out of 100. 100% is the whole amount. 50% is a half, 25% is a quarter, 10% is a tenth and 1% is a hundredth.

PercentageFractionHow to find it
50%12÷ 2
25%14÷ 4
10%110÷ 10
5%120half of 10%
1%1100÷ 100

Build any percentage from 10%, 5% and 1%

Find 10% first. Then put the pieces together.

Example

Find 15% of 360.

10% of 360 = 36. 5% is half of 10% = 18. 15% = 10% + 5% = 36 + 18.

Answer: 54

Example

Find 35% of 80.

10% = 8, so 30% = 24. 5% = 4. 35% = 24 + 4.

Answer: 28

Example

Find 99% of 300.

1% of 300 = 3. 99% = 100% − 1% = 300 − 3.

Answer: 297

Percentages of measures and money

Change to a smaller unit first if it helps: 20% of 4 kg = 20% of 4,000 g = 800 g.

Example

A coat costs £60. It is 25% off. What is the sale price?

25% of £60 = £60 ÷ 4 = £15 off. £60 − £15.

Answer: £45

What percentage is it?

Write a fraction, then make the total 100.

To compare test results, change each score to a percentage: 17 out of 20 = 85% is better than 42 out of 50 = 84%.

faq.q: How do you find a percentage of an amount in Year 6?
faq.a: Find 10% by dividing by 10 and 1% by dividing by 100, then build the percentage you need. For example, 30% of 250 is 3 × 25 = 75.

faq.q: How do you work out 15% of 360?
faq.a: 10% of 360 is 36 and 5% is half of that, 18. So 15% = 36 + 18 = 54. Do not divide 360 by 15.

faq.q: Are percentages in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. Percentages of amounts appear on the arithmetic paper (for example 35% of 260) and in reasoning questions about sales, surveys and test scores.

faq.q: How do you work out what percentage one number is of another?
faq.a: Write it as a fraction and make the total 100. 12 out of 50 = 12/50 = 24/100 = 24%.

items.q: The bar shows 84 split into equal parts. What is 50% of 84?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 84 ÷ 2 = 42. Do not double, and do not take away 50.

items.q: The bar shows 60 split into equal parts. What is 25% of 60?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 60 ÷ 4 = 15. Not 60 ÷ 25: 25% is one quarter. 45 is the other 75%.

items.q: The bar shows 70 split into equal parts. What is 10% of 70?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 70 ÷ 10 = 7. 10% means divide by 10, not by 100, and not take away 10.

items.q: The bar shows 120 split into equal parts. What is 25% of 120?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 120 ÷ 4 = 30. 60 is 50%. 25% is half of that.

items.q: The bar shows 450 split into equal parts. What is 10% of 450?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 450 ÷ 10 = 45. 4.5 is 1%. 405 is the other 90%.
10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 0.9 would be 1%. Do not take away 10.
10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 3,200 ÷ 10 = 320. 32 would be 1%. 2,880 is the other 90%.
10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 46 ÷ 10 = 4.6. Move each digit one place to the right: 46 becomes 4.6.
1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 500 ÷ 100 = 5. 1% means divide by 100, not by 10. Do not take away 1.
1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 1,200 ÷ 100 = 12. 120 would be 10%.
1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 350 ÷ 100 = 3.5. 35 would be 10%. Move each digit two places to the right.
50% is a half, so divide by 2: 2,500 ÷ 2 = 1,250. 250 would be 10%. 5,000 is double, not half.
50% is a half, so divide by 2: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5. The answer does not have to be a whole number. Not 9 ÷ 50.
25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. 24 is 50%. A quarter is half of a half: 24 ÷ 2 = 12.
25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Not 200 ÷ 25 = 8, and not 200 − 25.
25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. 5 is 50%. Half of 5 is 2.5.
1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 80 ÷ 100 = 0.8. 8 would be 10%.
10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5. 0.05 would be 1%. 10% is less than the number, not more.
25% is one quarter, so divide by 4: 64 ÷ 4 = 16. 64 ÷ 25 mixes up the 25 with the number of parts.
1% is one hundredth, so divide by 100: 700 ÷ 100 = 7. 700 ÷ 10 = 70 is 10%.

items.q: The bar shows 360 split into ten parts of 10%. What is 15% of 360?
items.e: 10% of 360 is 360 ÷ 10 = 36. 5% is half of 10%: 18. 15% = 10% + 5% = 36 + 18 = 54. Not 360 ÷ 15 = 24: that would split 360 into 15 parts. Not 15 × 360 either.
10% of 65 is 65 ÷ 10 = 6.5. 40% = 4 × 6.5 = 26. 39 is the other 60%. Do not take away 40.
90% = 100% − 10%. 10% is 70 ÷ 10 = 7. 70 − 7 = 63. 7 is the 10% you take away. Do not take away 10.

items.q: Jack works out 15% of 80 like this: 10% of 80 is 8, so 15% is 8 + 5 = 13. What is the correct answer?
Which is not a correct way to find 15% of 360?

sets.title: Percentages of measures: kg, m, litres and time

items.q: What is 20% of 4 kg? Give your answer in grams.
What is 30% of 2.5 m? Give your answer in centimetres.
What is 10% of 3 litres? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 3 litres = 3,000 ml. 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 3,000 ml ÷ 10 = 300 ml. 30 ml would be 1%. 1 litre = 1,000 ml, so 3 litres = 3,000 ml.

items.q: What is 50% of 1.5 km? Give your answer in metres.
items.e: 1.5 km = 1,500 m. 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 1,500 m ÷ 2 = 750 m. 0.75 km = 750 m, because 1 km = 1,000 m. Half, not double.

items.q: What is 75% of 1 litre? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 1 litre = 1,000 ml. 50% is 1,000 ml ÷ 2 = 500 ml. 25% is half of that: 250 ml. 75% = 50% + 25% = 500 ml + 250 ml = 750 ml. 250 ml is only 25%. Do not take away 75.

items.q: What is 15% of 2 m? Give your answer in centimetres.
What is 1% of 5 km? Give your answer in metres.
items.e: 5 km = 5,000 m. 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 5,000 m ÷ 100 = 50 m. 500 m would be 10%. 0.05 is in km: 0.05 km = 50 m.

items.q: What is 35% of 3 kg? Give your answer in grams.
What is 45% of 1.2 m? Give your answer in centimetres.
items.e: 1.2 m = 120 cm. 10% of 120 cm is 120 cm ÷ 10 = 12 cm. 40% = 4 × 12 cm = 48 cm. 5% is half of 10%: 6 cm. 45% = 40% + 5% = 48 cm + 6 cm = 54 cm. 48 cm is only 40%. 66 cm is the other 55%.

items.q: What is 65% of 2 litres? Give your answer in millilitres.
What is 40% of 2.5 kg? Give your answer in grams.

items.e: 10% of 80 cm is 80 cm ÷ 10 = 8 cm. 40% = 4 × 8 cm = 32 cm. Not 80 ÷ 40, and not 80 − 40. 48 cm is the other 60%.
10% of 250 ml is 250 ml ÷ 10 = 25 ml. 60% = 6 × 25 ml = 150 ml. 100 ml is the other 40%. 25 ml is only 10%.
10% of 50 kg is 50 kg ÷ 10 = 5 kg. 1% is 50 kg ÷ 100 = 0.5 kg, so 2% = 2 × 0.5 kg = 1 kg. 12% = 10% + 2% = 5 kg + 1 kg = 6 kg. 5 kg is only 10%: add 2% (1 kg) as well.

items.q: What is 25% of 1 hour? Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 25% is a quarter: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so 25% is not 25 minutes. 45 minutes is 75%.

items.q: What is 90% of 2 hours? Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 2 hours = 120 minutes. 10% is 12 minutes, so 90% = 120 − 12 = 108 minutes. 12 minutes is the 10% you take away.

items.q: Which is more: 20% of 3 kg or 70% of 800 g?
items.e: 20% of 3 kg: 3 kg = 3,000 g, 10% is 300 g, so 20% is 600 g. 70% of 800 g: 10% is 80 g, so 70% is 560 g. 600 g > 560 g, so 20% of 3 kg is more.

items.q: Which is the same as 30% of 2 m?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. 10% of 200 cm is 20 cm, so 30% is 3 × 20 = 60 cm. 6 cm uses 1 m = 10 cm. 140 cm is the other 70%.

sets.title: What percentage is it? Compare with percentages

Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 920 = 45100 = 45%. 9% would be 9 out of 100. 55% is the other part.
Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 25: 34 = 75100 = 75%. Do not write the 3 and the 4 together. 25% is the other quarter.

Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 20: 15 = 20100 = 20%. Do not write the 1 and the 5 together. 5% would be 1 out of 20.

items.q: What percentage of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts and 3 are shaded: 310 = 30100 = 30%. Each part is 10%, not 1%. 70% is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: What percentage of the grid is shaded?
items.e: 7 of the 20 squares are shaded. Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 720 = 35100 = 35%. There are 20 squares, not 100, so it is not 7%. 65% is not shaded.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 65%?
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 65% > 60%, so 65% is greater.
Change them all to percentages: 0.7 = 70%, 34 = 75%. 75% is the largest, so 34.
Change them all to percentages: 25 = 40%, 0.45 = 45%, 12 = 50%. The smallest is 38%.

items.q: Team A won 12 out of 20 matches. Team B won 14 out of 25 matches. Which team won the higher percentage of its matches?
items.e: Team A: 1220 = 60100 = 60%. Team B: 1425 = 56100 = 56%. 60% > 56%, so Team A, even though Team B won more matches.

items.q: Oliver scored 17 out of 20 in maths, 22 out of 25 in science and 43 out of 50 in English. In which test did he get the highest percentage?
items.e: Maths: 1720 = 85100 = 85%. Science: 2225 = 88100 = 88%. English: 4350 = 86100 = 86%. Science is highest, even though English has the most marks.

items.q: Noah got 18 out of 20 in a quiz. Ava got 45 out of 50 in a different quiz. Who got the higher percentage?
items.e: Noah: 1820 = 90100 = 90%. Ava: 4550 = 90100 = 90%. The percentages are equal, even though Ava has more marks.

sets.title: Percentage word problems: sales, surveys, tests and recipes

items.q: A coat costs £60. In the sale it is 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% is a quarter: £60 ÷ 4 = £15 off. Sale price: £60 − £15 = £45. £15 is the discount, not the price. Do not take away 25.

items.q: Trainers cost £80. They are 15% off. How much money is taken off?
items.e: 10% of £80 is £8 and 5% is £4, so 15% is £12. £68 is the sale price, not the money taken off.

items.q: A video game costs £45. It is reduced by 20%. What is the new price?
items.e: 10% of £45 is £4.50, so 20% is £9. New price: £45 − £9 = £36. £40.50 only takes off 10%. Do not take away 20.

items.q: Grace wants a £45 game. One shop offers 20% off. Another shop offers £10 off. Which is the better offer?
items.e: 20% of £45 = £9 off. £10 off saves more than £9, so £10 off is the better offer. 20% is not the same as £20 or £10.

items.q: Jeans cost £36 in two shops. Shop A takes 25% off. Shop B takes £8 off. Which shop is cheaper now?
items.e: Shop A: 25% of £36 = £9 off, so £27. Shop B: £36 − £8 = £28. £27 < £28, so Shop A is cheaper.

items.q: A bike was £240. The price is reduced by 30%. What is the new price?
items.e: 10% of £240 is £24, so 30% is £72 off. New price: £240 − £72 = £168. £72 is the discount. £216 only takes off 10%.

items.q: A jumper cost £50. In the sale it costs £40. What percentage has been taken off?
items.e: £10 has been taken off. 1050 = 20100 = 20%. The £10 is not 10%. Compare with the old price (£50), not the new price (£40).

items.q: A tablet costs £300. The price goes up by 5%. What is the new price?
items.e: 10% of £300 is £30, so 5% is £15. The price goes up: £300 + £15 = £315. Do not add £5, and do not take the £15 away.

items.q: Evie saves 10% of her £8 pocket money each week. How much does she save in 4 weeks?
items.e: 10% of £8 is 80p each week. In 4 weeks: 4 × 80p = 320p = £3.20. 80p is only one week.

items.q: A school trip costs £24. Parents pay 75% and the school pays the rest. How much do parents pay?
items.e: 50% of £24 is £12 and 25% is £6, so 75% is £12 + £6 = £18. £6 is what the school pays.

items.q: In a survey, 200 pupils chose their favourite sport. 35% chose football. How many pupils chose football?
items.e: 10% of 200 is 20, so 30% is 60, and 5% is 10. 35% = 60 + 10 = 70 pupils. 35 would be 35 out of 100, but there are 200 pupils.

items.q: 80 children were asked about their favourite fruit. 45% chose apples. How many children chose apples?
items.e: 10% of 80 is 8, so 40% is 32, and 5% is 4. 45% = 32 + 4 = 36 children. 44 is the other 55%.

items.q: There are 60 pupils in Year 6. 45% of them are girls. How many boys are there?
items.e: 45% of 60: 10% is 6, 40% is 24, 5% is 3, so 27 girls. Boys: 60 − 27 = 33. (Or 55% of 60 = 33.) 27 is the number of girls.

items.q: George scored 34 out of 40 in a spelling test. What percentage did he score?
items.e: 3440: divide the top and bottom by 4 to get 1720, then multiply the top and bottom by 5: 85100 = 85%. 15% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: Mohammed scored 18 out of 25 in maths and 34 out of 50 in science. In which test did he get the higher percentage?
items.e: Maths: 1825 = 72100 = 72%. Science: 3450 = 68100 = 68%. 72% > 68%, so maths, even though science has more marks.

items.q: A cake recipe uses 250 g of sugar. Isla uses 40% less sugar. How much sugar does she use?
items.e: 10% of 250 g is 25 g, so 40% is 100 g. Isla uses 250 g − 100 g = 150 g. 100 g is the sugar left out, not the sugar used.

items.q: A smoothie is 60% milk. How much milk is in 750 ml of smoothie?
items.e: 10% of 750 ml is 75 ml, so 60% is 6 × 75 = 450 ml. 300 ml is the other 40%. Do not take away 60.

items.q: Kai has a 1.5 litre bottle of water. He drinks 30% of it. How much water does he drink?
items.e: 1.5 litres = 1,500 ml. 10% is 150 ml, so 30% is 450 ml. 1,050 ml is what is left.

items.q: A football stadium holds 40,000 people. It is 85% full. How many people are in the stadium?
A charity needs £3,000. Ruby raises 4% of it. How much does she raise?
